name: Lauren Manoogian
band_note: mean of blouse and sweater entry $510 (women's price pass, 2026-10-13)
why: Women's knitwear, alpaca and wool layers, tailoring, dresses and shoes, mostly $490–$1,250, plus a small men's and home range, sold through its own site and New York store.

quote.q: A perceptible hand is maintained, where irregularities and non-uniformity are not just allowed but honored.

opview: “A perceptible hand is maintained, where irregularities and non-uniformity are not just allowed but honored.” — Lauren Manoogian (house), About, laurenmanoogian.com

facts_read.source: brand site (about, AW26 lookbook and collection, store, terms); nordstrom.com search; Vinted catalogue + item page; TRR designer index (2026-10-13 list); B Lab directory; GOTS database

Sweater.hp: SOFT CREWNECK (alpaca blended cashmere; regular, marked to $500)

doors.note: US: 1 own door, 407 Broome Street, New York 10013 (Nolita/SoHo), open to the public with appointment booking. No other store anywhere on the site and no stockist list published. Brand mark is LAUREN MANOOGIAN.

fibre.sample: stratified sample of 80 of 169 women's clothing styles (481 feed records; range = clothing product types that sit in the women's Outer/Top/Bottom/Dress collecti

craft_evidence.owned: claim, not shown — 'the brand operates between New York and Peru'; no workshop named or photographed on the pages read
craft_evidence.mills: no — fibre grades named (Super Baby Alpaca, Suri Alpaca, Pima cotton, Mulberry silk), no spinner or mill
craft_evidence.madein: ~83% (66 of 80 sampled PDPs: 'MADE IN PERU' on most knits, 'MADE IN JAPAN' on wovens)
craft_evidence.heritage: dated — 'Since 2008', led by Lauren Manoogian and partner Chris Fireoved, New York and Peru
craft_evidence.process: partial — a HANDKNIT line by name; 'a perceptible hand is maintained, where irregularities are honored'; no process page
craft_evidence.reasoning: Over four in five product pages state the country (Peru for knits, Japan for wovens), the about page dates the house to 2008 and says it operates between New York and Peru, and a hand-knit line is named. But no maker, mill or workshop is named or shown, so it sits on the 2/3 line; 3 if the Peru operation can be shown to be the brand's own.
